purpose: Review Estal-Mercado's Daniog River inventory as a potential freshwater source for Caraga. Preserve the printed labels and sampling scope while recording internal conflicts and withholding unverified taxon/site assertions.

studySource.author: Rozette Estal-Mercado
studySource.title: A Freshwater Fish Inventory of Daniog River, Lanuza, Surigao del Sur, Philippines
studySource.citation: Estal-Mercado, R. (2018). A Freshwater Fish Inventory of Daniog River, Lanuza, Surigao del Sur, Philippines. Science International (Lahore), 30(1), 141-145.
studySource.studyArea: Daniog River, Municipality of Lanuza, Surigao del Sur, Caraga, Philippines. The paper describes upper, middle and lower stream study sites.
studySource.coordinateUse: One locator for the study area, not three station coordinates. The article does not print hemisphere, datum, uncertainty or a taxon-to-point crosswalk; no geometry is derived.

samplingPeriodConflict.decision: Keep both source statements; do not normalize to one sampling period without clarification.

methods.reported: The abstract says local fishers used net fishing, scoop net, harpooning, traps, cast nets and angling at three river sites. The paper reports pH, dissolved oxygen and water temperature measurements.
notReportedOrUnclear: Sampling effort, number of visits, and effort per gear/site are not adequately specified in the reviewed text.
No salinity measurements are reported, so the paper's freshwater characterization does not resolve whether all three reaches are fresh or include tidal/brackish influence.

No specimen voucher accessions, collection repository, diagnostic identification protocol, or specimen-to-site crosswalk are reported; the table only cites FishBase and an aquarium/breeding reference as identification resources.
One study-area coordinate is supplied without hemispheres, datum, uncertainty, or site-level mapping precision.

sourceTable.tableHeading: List of fish species and abundance of the three representative site of Daniog River during July to December, 2017.
sourceSpellingFlags: Channa striate is retained verbatim; the spelling is not silently corrected.
Several family names are misspelled or outdated in the source table; no family-level normalization is made in this source review.

abundanceCountConflict.decision: Do not use the conflicting Site 1 count as an admitted or reconciled observation. The table describes means per sampling for species rows but does not explain the site-total aggregation clearly.

evidenceDecision.localityEvidence: Historical source-level report that fish were collected at a three-site Daniog River survey in 2016-2017; no independently verified voucher or precise station records are available in this review.
evidenceDecision.taxonEvidence: A separate bounded CAS Catalog cross-check proposes name/synonym/spelling crosswalks for the 11 binomials and flags two major locality mismatches; no specimen was reidentified. Retain all 13 original table labels as research candidates only.
evidenceDecision.dietEvidence: None. The article does not present stomach-content or prey-composition results.
evidenceDecision.waterQualityEvidence: Historical pH, dissolved oxygen and temperature measurements only; not current water quality or a safety advisory.
evidenceDecision.legalOrCatchabilityEvidence: None. The paper does not establish current fishing permissions, legal size/season rules or catchability.
evidenceDecision.rights: No item-specific open license or Bangwit publication permission was verified.

limitations: The study is historical and a single river survey; it does not provide a current, complete Daniog River checklist.
Sampling-period statements conflict between the abstract and Table 2 heading.
Site 1 totals conflict between narrative text and the table (205 versus 225 individuals).
Two labels stop at genus; a separate name-status review flags likely spelling/synonym changes and two major locality mismatches, but all specimens remain unverified.
No salinity is given; the paper's freshwater wording cannot be generalized across a potentially tidal river reach.
No sample effort, station-level coordinates, vouchers, or detailed identification protocol were found in the reviewed text.
No diet, bait, current safety, legal rule, current presence or public app claim is supported by this source alone.
nextAction: Seek voucher/depository details or author clarification for Mugil curema, Proterorhinus semilunaris and the printed Channa striate label; otherwise keep all 13 labels research-only and continue with a separate Daniog-area primary source review.

references.supports: Publisher-hosted primary article text, abstract, one study-area locator, three site labels, method summary, Table 2 labels/counts and internal date/count conflicts.
Author-upload discovery record only; this repository DOI is not treated as the journal article DOI or a license.
